steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Minimalism uses repetitive patterns that change GRADUALLY — tiny alterations accumulate into significant musical transformation over time. | Key Fact: Reich's phase shifting involves identical patterns starting together then gradually moving out of sync — creating complex textures from simple material. | Key Fact: Minimalist harmony often centres on a single chord or slow-moving progression — harmonic stasis focuses attention on rhythm, texture and timbre. | Key Fact: Technology enabled minimalist techniques: Reich's tape loops, Riley's keyboard delays, Adams' digital processing all expand what is possible with repetition.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
